first.rationale: Simplifying onboarding currently best addresses both the 4% completion decline and the 6% activation decline, with prior evidence of durable activation and adoption gains. Verify memory_86 to assess whether those gains translated into qualified long-term revenue, and memory_73 because promotional pricing is the strongest competing response but may carry discounting, retention, or customer-quality risk not resolved by the summary.

final.rationale: Run a standard experiment shortening onboarding. Verified evidence shows completion increased 13%, time-to-value improved by 2.1 days, and 30-day retention rose 3%, directly addressing the current completion and activation declines while supporting sustainability. Promotional pricing is rejected because its 18% qualified-revenue lift came with a 12% retention decline and failure through the first renewal cycle. Measure qualified revenue and longer-term retention because onboarding evidence remains strongest on intermediate and 30-day outcomes rather than long-term revenue.
